instruction.text: What are the bolded verb(s) in the following sentence doing? Select the correct answer.

atoms.a: Can you promise me that you’ll keep this secret?

correct.text: Correct! The interrogative mood is used to ask questions. To make questions, we often put the verb before the subject. If there is a question word (who, what, when or how) at the beginning, the verb comes after it.
correct.sound: Correct! The interrogative mood is used to ask questions. To make questions, we often put the verb before the subject. If there is a question word (such as. who, what, when or how) at the beginning, the verb comes after it.

feedback.correct: Correct! The imperative mood is used to order someone to do something, give instructions, offer advice or make suggestions. The imperative usually doesn’t have a subject and uses the infinitive form of a verb without to.

atoms.a: She dropped me off at practice and told me she would be back in two hours.

feedback.correct: Correct! The indicative mood is used to express facts, statements or opinions. This is the most common verb mood.

atoms.a: He told me he would like to go to dinner with me.

feedback.correct: The conditional mood is used to make requests and to refer to situations which may be uncertain. The conditional is formed by using the verb would or should and the infinitive of another verb.

atoms.a: He wishes he felt more comfortable in his skin.

correct.text: The subjunctive mood is used to express a wish or possibility. The subjunctive form of a verb is made up of the 3rd person present singular without the endings -s or -es.
correct.sound: The subjunctive mood is used to express a wish or possibility. The subjunctive form of a verb is made up of the 3rd person present singular without the endings -s or -e s.
